title: Low-to-high software and model promotion with reusable accreditation, low-SWaP software-defined cross-domain at the edge, and bridging BICES intelligence to MPE mission-command networks
problem: Moving containerized applications, ML models and intelligence products across classification and coalition boundaries (unclassified factories to Secret/TS, tactical guards for voice/video/ML outputs, BICES to MPE) depends on approved media, NCDSMO-baselined guards and per-program re-accreditation, so every classified update or cross-enclave product is slow, manual and program-specific.
echelons: enterprise software factory (AFLCMC/Platform One, service factories)
program office / ISSM on SIPR-JWICS enclaves
tactical CDS operator (platform, expeditionary targeting cell)
coalition intelligence cell (G2/J2, US BICES, MPE)

user.echelon: Enterprise (AFLCMC, DISA, SAF/CDM) down to division/corps G2 and platform-level tactical CDS

current_workflow: Build and harden on the low side (Iron Bank / Platform One / service factory).
Package (e.g., Zarf bundle) and either burn to approved media or submit through an NCDSMO-listed CDS with content inspection.
Manually import on the high side, re-scan, re-run STIG/compliance checks, re-register images in a high-side registry.
Update the classified ATO/eMASS package for the enclave; repeat for every release.

For a new tactical data type (voice, video, FMV, ML output): program requests a filter from the CDS vendor, vendor develops, NSA/NCDSMO assesses, filter fields later via sole-source IDIQ modification.
For coalition intelligence: analyst views BICES separately, then re-creates or re-marks relevant products on the MPE (REL NATO) network using a different tool.
current_solution: Platform One / Iron Bank replicated to Secret (2023) with TS planned; Second Front Game Warden and Palantir PFCS Forward / FedStart for classified hosting; hyperscaler Secret/TS regions under JWCC; Zarf / UDS (Defense Unicorns) for air-gap packaging; NCDSMO-listed guards from Everfox, Owl (V2CDS, XD Vision, CDFMV), GDMS (TACDS, BICES TNE CDS), Northrop, Lockheed (Radiant Mercury); PMAT Tactical Edge Nodes; DISA CDES; for BICES-MPE, no automated bridge - human re-posting and LNOs.
failure: Every hop is a human-mediated transfer with duplicated scanning and re-accreditation; new cross-domain data types wait on vendor filter development and NSA lab assessment delivered through sole-source vehicles; BICES and MPE are separately governed and accredited (NATO BICES Group Executive vs DISA), so intelligence never reaches mission-command tools automatically.

evidence.claim: NSA NCDSMO 'Raise the Bar' (first published 2018; RTB baseline v4.1 dated 2022-07-11) applies to all CDS protecting classified information; NIST SP 800-53 AC-4(20) requires use of solutions on the NCDSMO baseline list, i.e., only listed CDS may be used - a structural gate for any new entrant.
evidence.source_title: NSA Cross Domain Solutions resource page; CSF Tools AC-4(20); NIST CSRC glossary 'cross domain baseline list'
evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The core product (a guard or promotion path that moves data across classification boundaries) must pass NSA/NCDSMO lab assessment against Raise the Bar and be baseline-listed before any DoD site may use it (AC-4(20)); that takes years, cleared U.S.-citizen staff, a facility clearance and a sponsoring program, and the resulting market is small (DISA CDES procurement lines historically ~$1-2M/yr) and served through sole-source IDIQs (Owl, GDMS, Everfox, Lockheed, Northrop). The venture-scale adjacent slot (air-gap packaging and classified hosting) is already held by cleared U.S. firms - Defense Unicorns ($136M Series B, Jan 2026), Second Front, Palantir - and by government-owned Platform One. The BICES-MPE bridge is an inter-governmental (NATO BGX vs DISA) accreditation and policy decision, not a product gap. Startups have not solved it because the parts that are solvable by software are commoditised or government-owned, and the parts that are not are legally gated.
technical_wedge: No credible standalone wedge for this team. The only defensible adjacencies are (a) low-side 'promotion-ready' packaging and attestation content (SBOM, OSCAL evidence, signed Zarf/OCI bundles with policy metadata) that a high-side operator or CDS filter consumes, and (b) authoring filter/data-format descriptions (e.g., DFDL schemas, ACP-240/ZTDF tagging profiles) as a subcontractor to a listed CDS vendor. Both are content or services, not a product with pricing power, and both are already served by open source (Zarf, UDS, Lula, OpenTDF) or by the vendors themselves.

mvp.what: An unclassified reference pipeline that emits signed, policy-annotated container/model bundles with machine-readable evidence (SBOM, STIG results, OSCAL component definitions) and a simulated one-way transfer to a mock 'high side' registry that verifies provenance and re-imports without human re-scan.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes as a demo; it proves nothing that a CDS buyer or AO needs, because acceptance depends on an NCDSMO-listed guard and an AO's risk decision, neither of which the MVP can exercise.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That a high-side operator would accept low-side evidence in lieu of re-scanning (a policy decision, not a technical one) and that a listed CDS vendor would adopt the bundle format as a filter target - both require access the team does not have.

data_requirement.what: Real CDS filter specifications (on Intelink/NCDSMO, classified or CUI), enclave ATO packages, actual BICES/MPE product formats and releasability rules.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: No for the core: NCDSMO requirements and vendor SDKs are not public and access requires clearance and sponsorship; public STIG, OSCAL, DFDL, ACP-240 and OpenTDF material is obtainable for the adjacency only.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (13 CFR 121.702); the Indonesian founder's shares never count and the German founder's only after the green card issues. CDS work is export-controlled (NSA RTB covers all CDS sold for export) and classified-dependent; personnel clearances require U.S. citizenship (E07-F21), so neither founder can work on the product's core. FOCI (32 CFR 117.11) treats any non-citizen owner as a foreign interest; a facility clearance would need cleared U.S.-citizen key management and FOCI mitigation. All of this needs export-control and security counsel; no legal judgment is made here.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: They largely already have it or are inside the moat: Palantir runs PFCS Forward/FedStart at IL6; L3Harris and GDMS/Lockheed/Northrop hold listed guards; Defense Unicorns and Second Front own the air-gap and hosting slots; Platform One is government-owned and free to programs. Anduril would partner with a listed CDS vendor rather than build one.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: REJECT. There is no unlisted, unclassified surface where a startup can accumulate an advantage; any progress a startup made in filter content or packaging would be absorbed by the listed vendor that owns the interface and the sole-source vehicle.

regulatory_burden.explanation: NSA/NCDSMO lab assessment and baseline listing (AC-4(20)); NIAP/CSfC where applicable; classified enclave ATOs; ITAR/EAR treatment of CDS (RTB explicitly covers CDS sold for export); FOCI under 32 CFR 117.11 and DoDI 5205.87; personnel clearances requiring U.S. citizenship. Every element is a hard gate, not a compliance cost.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The non-U.S.-person co-founder could not access CDS technical data, filter SDKs or classified requirements; the German founder is not clearance-eligible until citizenship. A permanent-resident owner is still a 'foreign interest' for FOCI. Product-core work would have to be done entirely by cleared U.S.-citizen hires the founders cannot supervise on technical substance. Needs export-control and security counsel; no legal judgment is made here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Cross-domain guards and classified promotion have no meaningful commercial market; the nearest analogues (OT data diodes, regulated-industry air-gap delivery) are small and already served by Owl, Waterfall and cloud vendors. Air-gap packaging tooling is open source (Zarf).

defensibility.explanation: For whoever holds it, an NCDSMO listing plus program-embedded deployments is one of the strongest moats in defense IT (sole-source IDIQs, decade-long sustainment). For this team the moat is unreachable, so defensibility scores well as a property of the gap and zero as a property of the founders.

why_now: 2022 cATO memo, 2025 CSRMC tenets (reciprocity, inheritance, automation), Platform One's Secret expansion (2023-2025), DISA's data-centric MPE/CIE strategy (2026) and MPE accreditation for NATO Secret intelligence (2024-2025) all make automated promotion and coalition bridging conceivable; Defense Unicorns' $136M raise (Jan 2026) shows investors agree - but every 'why now' factor benefits cleared incumbents and government-owned platforms rather than a new, non-cleared entrant.
killer_risk: The founding team cannot legally or practically work on the product's core: NCDSMO listing, classified enclave access, export-control on CDS and U.S.-citizenship clearance rules exclude both founders, and the parts that remain unclassified (packaging, tagging content) are open source or owned by the listed vendor that controls the interface and the sole-source vehicle.

allied_extension: Marginally: allied CDS markets (UK, Germany, NATO) have their own national accreditation bodies and incumbents (Garrison, Everfox, secunet, Rohde & Schwarz - RECALL, not re-verified this session), and NATO's Rapid Adoption Action Plan (Jun 2025) eases prototype-to-buy for demonstrated software. A German founder could in principle pursue a German-accredited product for Bundeswehr or NATO use, but that is a different company with the same certification economics, and it would not transfer to the U.S. market (RTB also governs CDS sold for export). The BICES-MPE bridge is decided by NATO BGX and DISA, not by vendors.
